name: @jipika/dsh-memory
description: Progressive long-term memory for DSH: sharded markdown bodies under ~/.dsh/memory/topics/, with only a live-generated index (shard · count · path · per-entry line numbers) injected into the system prompt — so the prompt cost stays flat however large the memory grows. Two layers (global + per-project) plus the global rule files, viewable AND editable in DSH Settings, with per-layer switches and an index/full injection toggle. v0.5.0 adds enforcement hooks: a write guard on the native tool pipeline (format/secrets/history rules, optional external command judge, deny/ask with reasons fed back to the model), post-write audit log, a read reminder when memory files are read, a mandatory discipline block, and an optional injection filter command. Zero extra LLM cost, live re-read. v0.5.1 keeps the switches in ~/.dsh/memory/settings.json — read live by the plugin and edited from the settings pane over the plugin's own route, independent of the host settings API. v0.6.0 fixes the index silently degrading to a title-less directory once memory outgrew the hardcoded 9k budget (which is why an agent could see memory injected and still never read it): the index now shrinks per-shard along a newest-N-per-shard ladder under a configurable indexBudget, adds per-shard keywords (routing hint) and latest-entry dates, ships a 'check memory before starting a task' discipline, and makes full mode read the shard bodies (auto-falling back to index when over budget) instead of the retired memory.md navigation file.
